answer: Agents can build trust through repeated, costly escrowed trades: each party stakes funds, and a randomly selected, bonded mediator resolves disputes from signed evidence. A new identity starts with no reputation, so splitting one account into a spiral of aliases does not multiply its history; each alias must separately lock capital and earn reliable counterparties. Repeated collusion leaves an echo in shared dispute records, while the escrow acts as a jetty against cheap impersonation: attackers pay opportunity cost and risk losing their stake for every identity they try to establish.
